storyBibleReview.topicQuestion: How can a loose bag move from a street into a stream?
storyBibleReview.progression: Follow one empty bag from a street, across grass, briefly onto a branch, then into a stream; wind and flowing water move it through different places.
storyBibleReview.synthesis: Wind and moving water can carry loose litter away from the place it was left.

scienceSources.title: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency: Learn About Aquatic Trash
scienceSources.evidence: Loose litter can be carried by wind and water from land into streams and rivers. This book follows one illustrative route, without claiming every item takes that route or reaches the ocean.

storyBibleReview.factualScope: One possible litter journey in specific wind and stream conditions. Not all plastic floats forever or reaches the sea. No removal, harm or moral claim is added in place of the physical explanation.

pages.text: The bag blows across the grass.

pages.imageAlt: The bag moves over the grass toward a low branch.

pages.state: Bag farther from street and closer to branch; still airborne.

pages.text: It catches on a low branch.

pages.pageDescription: One bag handle catches on the end of the branch.

pages.text: The wind pulls the bag free.

pages.imageBrief: Bag lands partly on the shallow flowing stream surface beside the bank. Body still holds some air, one edge touching water with tiny ripples; no creature beneath it or new deep ocean.

pages.pageDescription: The yellow bag lands in the stream.

pages.text: The stream carries the bag away.

pages.imageAlt: Flowing water carries the bag along the stream.
pages.pageDescription: Flowing water carries the bag along the stream.
pages.state: Bag transported downstream by flowing water; no change into sinking rock.

pages.text: Wind and water can move trash.
pages.imageBrief: One coherent wide landscape joins distant street at left, grass and branch in middle, stream with the single bag farther right. No repeated bags, montage or map. The final position visibly differs from the first.
pages.imageAlt: The street and branch lie behind the bag as it travels down the stream.
pages.pageDescription: The street and branch lie behind the bag as it travels down the stream.

character.evidence: One empty bag travels from a particular street across grass, catches on a low branch and enters a nearby stream.

goal.evidence: The opening locates the litter. The inquiry about how it moves develops from the first gust rather than a stated question.

causality.evidence: Wind lifts and transports the bag, a branch briefly holds it, another gust frees it, and flowing water continues the journey.

obstacle.evidence: A temporary snag and a change from air to water reveal two physical agents without replacing explanation with a moral slogan.

agency.evidence: Each page changes position or force; the branch pause and release make the route worth following.

ending.evidence: Wind and water can move trash combines both observed parts of the route while preserving the possibility word can.

language.evidence: Short concrete clauses with wind/stream/trash preparation fit A. Pronoun it always refers to the same single bag.

voice.evidence: Lifts, blows, catches, pulls, falls and carries form a natural action sequence; the tone is observational.

delight.evidence: Following the same bag through a snag and a new moving medium creates mild suspense and a useful rereading route.

canon.evidence: Independent sequence confirms one pale-yellow two-handled bag with its identifying notch, continuous street/grass/branch/stream route, correct handle snag/release and downstream travel.

illustration.evidence: Airborne, caught, released and floating states stay distinct, with no invented drain, second bag or unexplained reversal. The final wide route contains only one bag downstream. Current independent sequence is clear.

audio.evidence: All 9 exact current title/page texts have hash-matching Leda clips in the automated narration report, with full decode/signal and independent-recognition dispositions. Shared word reuse is governed by the cohort inventory. Automated evidence supports a sound current recording set; reader playback remains separate, so fully verified score 4 is not assigned. No human-listening claim.
